description:
## Site
apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex restore_queued_to_editor/2:

\`\`\`elixir
input = %{state.input | value: combined, cursor: String.length(combined)}
\`\`\`

This blasts a new value into the input struct directly, bypassing
\`Components.Input.set_value/2\` which knows about cursor clamping
and the input's internal contract.

## Change
\`\`\`elixir
input =
  state.input
  |> Components.Input.set_value(combined)
  |> Map.put(:cursor, String.length(combined))
\`\`\`

(set_value clamps cursor to min(c, length(value)); we then push it
to the end manually since we want the cursor placed AFTER the
restored text.)

Same treatment for the streaming-submit clause in do_handle_submit
which directly does \`%{new_input | value: \"\", cursor: 0}\` —
\`Components.Input.set_value(new_input, \"\")\` does that and respects
input invariants.

## Tests
opi-tze.5 and opi-tze.2 tests already assert .value and .cursor;
they should keep passing. Adding tests for kill-ring / undo
preservation is a stretch; the primary win is honoring the abstraction.

## Why this isn't done in opi-tze
Cosmetic; deferred to keep opi-tze commits minimal.
title: Use Components.Input.set_value in restore_queued_to_editor
